ruleName: Actions That Improve Conditions Affecting the Stroke
title: Is it Allowed to Remove Dew or Frost from Your Line of Play?
question: Early on a cold morning, your ball is on the fairway. There is a layer of frost and dew on the grass between your ball and the hole. Before playing, you wipe the frost away with your towel to make the shot easier. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: This is allowed because dew and frost are temporary water.
This is allowed because you are only cleaning the grass.
You receive the general penalty because you improved the conditions affecting your stroke.

explanation: Dew, frost and water are not loose impediments, so you cannot deliberately remove them to improve the conditions affecting your stroke. Brushing away dew or frost from your line of play or the area where your club will swing is a breach of Rule 8. However, there is no penalty if you accidentally remove dew or frost while taking a normal stance or making your stroke.
